summary: Defines how the Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP), a method for carrying multiprotocol datagrams over point-to-point links, can be transported over ATM using the AAL2 adaptation layer.

plainLanguage.summary: PPP is a way to send data down a single wire. This document says how to do that on ATM networks that chop data into tiny cells.

questions: how does ppp run over atm aal2
how does aal2 reduce overhead for ppp
what are uui code points 26 and 27
ppp over aal2 vs ppp over aal5
subtitle: Carrying PPP over ATM AAL2 so that small packets such as voice waste less bandwidth than they do over AAL5.

tldr.problem: PPP over AAL5 is bandwidth inefficient for small payloads such as voice, especially when RTP header compression is used.
tldr.mechanism: PPP frames get a 16-bit CRC, are segmented with the AAL2 SSSAR sublayer and are multiplexed by the AAL2 CPS into ATM cells, using UUI code points 27 (more to come) and 26 (final).
tldr.outcome: Less per-packet overhead and no AAL5 padding when cells stay full. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 3336 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2002, and no later RFC obsoletes or updates it. A companion document, RFC 3337, covers class extensions using multiple AAL2 CIDs.

sections.title: Why PPP Over AAL2
sections.content:
The PPP over AAL5 encapsulation (RFC 2364) works well for IP but is bandwidth inefficient for small payloads such as voice, and more so when used with RTP header compression (RFC 2508).

PPP over AAL2 addresses this by using the AAL2 Common Part Sublayer (CPS) to multiplex several PPP payloads into a set of ATM cells. It is meant for implementations that want PPP facilities such as the Link Control Protocol, Network-layer Control Protocols, authentication and compression. Those need a point-to-point relationship between peers, so the design is not for the multi-point relationships available in ATM and other multi-access environments.
sections.plainLanguage: Sending a short message in its own big envelope wastes paper. AAL2 lets several short messages share one envelope.

sections.title: The AAL2 Service Interface
sections.content:
The PPP layer treats AAL2 as a bit-synchronous point-to-point link, and the PPP link corresponds to an ATM AAL2 virtual connection. That connection MUST be full-duplex and point to point. It MAY be dedicated (permanent, set up by provisioning) or switched (set up on demand).

  • The boundary is an octet interface; sub-octets are not supplied or accepted.
  • PPP imposes no restriction on the ATM traffic descriptor parameters.
  • The AAL2 layer MUST signal when the link is connected or disconnected, giving the "Up" and "Down" events to the LCP state machine. For PPP over AAL2, link state can be derived from type 3 fault management packets carried in-band within a given AAL2 CID flow.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP wants a private two-way phone line. AAL2 provides one, and tells PPP when the line is connected or has dropped.

sections.title: Encapsulation, Segmentation and CRC
sections.content:
PPP over AAL2 uses the AAL2 CPS unchanged. Because protocols such as RTP header compression need packet error detection, it adds a 16-bit CRC to each PPP frame and uses the Service Specific Segmentation and Reassembly Sublayer (SSSAR) of I.366.1 to send the packet as a series of AAL2 frames.

Each frame carries the PPP Protocol ID (8 or 16 bits), the Information field and the CRC-16. The CRC covers the Protocol ID and information field. Its algorithm is the same as the Frame Check Sequence of Q.921, with generator polynomial x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1. The register is preset to all ones, and the ones complement of the remainder goes in the CRC field.

The UUI field of the CPS packet marks segmentation. Code point 27 means a non-final fragment and 26 means the final fragment. An unsegmented packet therefore carries UUI 26. When a packet is segmented, the Protocol ID, Information and CRC-16 are split across several SSSAR frames.
sections.plainLanguage: A long letter is cut into pieces, and each piece is marked 'more coming' or 'last piece'. A check number at the end lets the receiver tell if anything got scrambled.

sections.title: Channel Identifiers and Operation
sections.content:
An implementation MAY use one or several AAL2 Channel Identifiers (CIDs) to carry PPP packets for a session. Both endpoints MUST agree on the number, SSCS mapping and values of the CIDs. The values come from static provisioning for a dedicated connection (PVC) or from Q.2630.2 signaling for a switched one (SPVC or SVC). A companion document, RFC 3337, describes class extensions that use multiple CIDs.

Other, non-PPP AAL2 users can share the same virtual connection on different CIDs, because multiple SSCS types can coexist in one AAL2 VCC.

In the RFC's worked example, an interface with RTP header compression sends compressible RTP packets to the compressor and everything else straight to PPP. PPP packets are then segmented with SSSAR, multiplexed by the CPS onto CPS-PDUs and passed to the ATM layer. The receiver reassembles packets, checks the CRC and hands them up by PPP payload type.

Implementations MUST meet all the requirements of PPP (RFC 1661). By default the 16-bit CRC encapsulation is used and the default Maximum-Receive-Unit is 1500 bytes.
sections.plainLanguage: Several lanes can share one road, and both ends must agree on which lane carries what before they start.

sections.title: Comparison with AAL5 Encapsulations
sections.content:
Over AAL2, the per-payload overhead is a 2-byte CRC, a 3-byte CPS header and a 1-byte Start Field, 6 bytes in total. PPP over AAL5 has an 8-byte AAL5 trailer. AAL2 multiplexing also removes AAL5's padding for short frames.

The RFC also compares PPP with PPPMUX (RFC 3153) over AAL5. PPPMUX multiplexes in the PPP layer, but its frames still need the 8-byte AAL5 trailer plus an average of 24 bytes of AAL5 PAD. With AAL2, as long as PPP frames reach the CPS before its TIMER_CU expires, cells are filled and no PAD is needed.

AAL2 also avoids delay and loss amplification. A PPPMUX receiver must reassemble a whole AAL5 frame, possibly many cells, before extracting payloads, and one lost cell discards the whole packet. The AAL2 CPS extracts each payload as it arrives, and a lost cell only loses the packets inside it.
sections.plainLanguage: Mailing each tiny note in its own box wastes space. Packing many notes into shared boxes, and unpacking each as it arrives, is faster and loses less if a box is dropped.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
As with any encapsulation, a receiver must be able to trust that the sender identified the encapsulated protocol correctly and that the transport network has not been compromised. PPP sessions follow the RFC 1661 state machine, which can require an authentication phase using PAP or CHAP before network-layer packets flow.

PPP-level authentication does not guard against man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker compromises the ATM switching network. Applications needing protection are encouraged to use authentication headers, encrypted payloads, or ATM-layer security services. Because non-PPP CIDs may share the same virtual connection, an endpoint cannot assume that PPP authentication also secures them.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP can check who is on the other end of the line, but that does not protect against someone tapping the line, or the other lanes sharing the road.
